core.title: Register a subject before typing any user/system flow under it
core.given: A plan contains a typed user/system flow (a user/system flow identity of subject plus slug, in the profile's user/system flow URN shape) or a subject entry in the subject registry
core.when: the planner types or re-identifies a user/system flow, edits the subject registry, or the plan reaches CONFIRM
core.then: Ensure the subject exists in the subject registry before any user/system flow is typed under it.
prefer: Add the subject entry to the subject registry first, then type user/system flows under it
Choose as subject the durable object the user/system flow changes, written as a kebab-case noun-led name (this naming is mandatory, see avoid[1])
Reuse an existing registered subject when the user/system flow changes the same durable object
avoid: Typing a user/system flow under an unregistered subject

Any subject (registry entry or typed user/system flow) that is not ALL of: kebab-case, noun-led, and the durable object of the user/system flow's change. This is mandatory, not a preference; camelCase/snake_case/other non-kebab names fail, and a verb, an actor, a theme, a route, a category, an owner or a program name is never a valid subject
Duplicate subject entries in the registry (registry entries are unique-by-subject)
Two typed user/system flows with the same subject+slug (typed user/system flows are unique-by-subject+slug)
Leaving an existing misnamed or duplicated subject/identity in place because the current edit did not change it; CONFIRM validates the whole registry
core.why: A user/system flow's identity is its subject plus slug, so the subject must be a registered, durable noun and identities must be unique for every typed user/system flow to resolve to exactly one stable subject.
evidence: The subject-registry invariant check passes at the CONFIRM phase
Every typed user/system flow in the plan has its subject present in the subject registry
Every registry and typed-train subject is kebab-case, noun-led and the durable object of the user/system flow's change (not a verb, actor, theme, route, category, owner or program name)
No duplicate subject in the registry and no duplicate subject+slug among typed user/system flows
On failure, evidence reports the subject, the slug and the registry status
verification: A registry-coherence check validates the whole subject registry and every typed user/system flow at the CONFIRM phase; it is confirm-blocking, so pre-existing violations also fail even when the current edit did not introduce them

The check covers: subject kebab-case and noun-led, the durable object of a user/system flow's change (not a verb/actor/theme/route/category/owner/program name); subject registered in the subject registry before the first user/system flow is typed under it; registry entries unique-by-subject; typed user/system flows unique-by-subject+slug
On failure, the finding reports the subject, the slug and the subject's registry status

Registration, kebab-case and duplicates are mechanically checkable once a diff-level observer for typed user/system flows and registry edits exists; noun-led durable object vs verb/actor/theme/route/category/owner/program name needs judgement (llm_judged)

values: user/system flow typed under a new or an existing subject
subject registry entry added, renamed or edited
user/system flow subject or slug changed
subject is not a noun-led durable object

fires: A plan types a user/system flow under a subject that is not in the subject registry
A plan types a new user/system flow under a subject that is already registered (naming and subject+slug uniqueness must still hold)
A planner adds, renames or edits an entry in the subject registry, independently of any user/system flow
A plan adds a second user/system flow with the same subject+slug as an existing typed user/system flow
A registry entry or typed user/system flow uses a subject that is not kebab-case, not noun-led, or is a verb, actor, theme, route, category, owner or program name
CONFIRM runs and the existing registry or typed user/system flows already violate naming, registration or uniqueness
doesNotFire: Changes outside the plan root that neither touch the subject registry nor type, rename or reference user/system flow identities, outside the CONFIRM validation run

profileRequirements.meaning: The root under which plan artifacts (typed user/system flows and the subject registry) live; the check scans plan files for typed user/system flows, and changes outside this root do not fire.
The single registry file in which every subject must be registered before any user/system flow is typed under it; registration, naming and uniqueness are all checked against it.
The syntax of a typed user/system flow identity (subject plus slug), by which typed user/system flows are recognised in plan files, planner tasks and user/system-flow-identity references.

neutralityNotes: Planner-method vocabulary kept in the core because it is ATDD-method-level, not stack-level: user/system flow, subject, slug, typed user/system flow, subject registry (as a concept), the CONFIRM phase, confirm-blocking enforcement, and the kebab-case noun-led durable-object naming rule. Stack-concrete data moved to the profile: the registry location (proposed layout.registries#subject_registry = plan/_subjects.yaml, under roots.plan = plan) and the user/system-flow-identity syntax (urn.user-system-flow = user-system-flow:<subject>:<slug>). Per-rule severity (4), disposition (strict), the confirm-blocking whole-registry scope and the failure-report fields stay in core verification; this rule's validator/template/variant/subject-kind ids remain bunOnly. The diff-level observer for typed user/system flows and registry edits (needs_new_observer) and the llm_judged noun-led-durable-object judgement are stated as observability/verification scope, not as implemented checks; nothing else could not be made neutral.
